cards.text: This song comes from Asaph, chief of the Levites David appointed to give thanks and praise before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). He opens STRONG: "Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart." Hold onto that line, friend, because we're coming back to it.

cards.question: Right after saying God is good, Asaph gets honest about himself. What does he admit?

answers.text: He had written his last song

cards.text: Here's where he almost slipped: Asaph looked around and saw the wicked doing GREAT. Prosperity everywhere he turned.

cards.question: When Asaph saw the prosperity of the wicked, he ___ the arrogant.

cards.text: Asaph is the guy stuck in traffic, scrolling everybody else's beach pictures. He says the wicked have no struggle in their death, and their bodies are well-fed.

cards.question: Asaph says the wicked are free of the ___ others carry.

cards.text: Asaph says pride is their necklace and a garment of violence covers them. They're not hiding it, friend, they're ACCESSORIZING.

cards.question: Out of their prosperity comes iniquity, and their imaginations run wild. Then these proud people open their mouths. What does Asaph say they do?
Asaph says these mocking people keep their big talk to themselves and leave heaven out of it.

cards.text: Not even close. They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth. STRUTTING tongues, friend. Somebody roll out a runway.

cards.question: Asaph says their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance. Then the wicked ask a question about God. What is it about?

cards.text: Asaph sums them up: always carefree, and their wealth keeps growing. I bet these folks have never set an alarm in their LIVES.

cards.question: Now Asaph looks at his own life. He's kept his heart pure and washed his hands in innocence. What does he say all that was?

cards.text: Picture following the cookie recipe to the letter while the guy next to you skips the oven and STILL takes home the blue ribbon. That's what Asaph's saying here.

cards.question: Asaph, the one who kept his heart pure, says his troubles show up every morning.

cards.text: So Asaph's got all these thoughts piling up about the wicked getting rich. But he knows what would happen if he started saying them out loud.

cards.question: Asaph says if he had decided to speak this way, something would have happened. What?

cards.text: So Asaph tries to work it all out, and it's troublesome in his sight. Lying awake, running the same question in circles, getting NOWHERE.

cards.question: Then the whole thing turns around for Asaph. Where does he go?
When Asaph entered God's sanctuary, he discerned the wicked people's ___.

cards.text: All that wrestling on his own, then one visit to God's sanctuary and Asaph SEES it. Trust me, I know what it's like when the light finally comes in and everything looks different.

cards.question: Asaph's own feet almost slipped. Now he says God has set the wicked on solid ground.

cards.text: It's slick ground, and God casts them down into ruin. Asaph says, "How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!"

cards.question: Asaph compares the Lord awakening and despising the form of the wicked to someone waking from a ___.

cards.text: You know that dream where everything's going your way, and then the alarm goes off? GONE. Asaph says, like one waking from a dream, the Lord awakens and despises their form.

cards.question: Asaph looks back at when his heart was grieved and he was pierced within. He says he was senseless and ___.

cards.text: He even calls himself a brute beast before God. Friend, I respect a man who roasts himself. I do it DAILY.

cards.question: Asaph says that after all his envy and confusion, God let go of him.

cards.text: Not for a second. Asaph says, "Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand."

cards.question: God holds Asaph's right hand. What else does Asaph say God does for him?

answers.text: Makes him rich like the wicked
Gives him a life with no trouble

cards.text: And later, God will receive him in glory. Then Asaph asks, "Whom have I in heaven but You?" and says on earth he desires no one besides God.

cards.question: Asaph says his flesh and his heart may ___, but God is the ___ of his heart and his portion forever.

cards.text: Asaph looks at the wicked one last time. Those far from God will surely perish, and God destroys all who are unfaithful to Him.

cards.question: Asaph started out saying God is good, then almost slipped. Where does he land at the end?

answers.text: It is good to draw near to God
It is better to be rich
It is safer to stay quiet

cards.text: He's made the Lord GOD his refuge, that he may proclaim all God's works. From almost slipping to SINGING about it, friend. Now THAT'S a comeback.

findings.problem: The question says Asaph 'gets honest about himself' and asks what he 'admits.' That rules out the wrong answer 'He had never once doubted' before the baker reasons anything out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Prosperity everywhere he turned' stretches Psalm 73:3, which says only that he saw the prosperity of the wicked. The line is told as part of the passage, not as a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The joke puts Asaph himself into the modern scene ('Asaph is the guy stuck in traffic, scrolling everybody else's beach pictures'). That blends the comparison with the Bible setting.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Psalm 73:7 ('From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild') is told only inside the choice card's question, and the card cites only 73:8. Verse 7 has no story card and no citation anywhere in the walkthrough.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: Psalm 73:10 ('their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance') is told only inside the choice card's question, and the card cites only 73:11. Verse 10 has no story card and no citation anywhere in the walkthrough.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: This story card only restates Psalm 73:13, which card 13 already covered, through a cookie comparison ('That's what Asaph's saying here'). It doesn't move the passage forward.
The statement says Asaph's 'troubles show up every morning.' Psalm 73:14 says he is 'punished every morning' and 'afflicted all day long.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'Lying awake' adds a time of day (night) that Psalm 73:16 doesn't give. It is told as a fact about Asaph.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: This story card re-tells Psalm 73:17, which cards 4 and 5 just covered, and adds nothing new from the passage.
'I know what it's like when the light finally comes in' calls back to the light in the junk drawer, a small drawer detail, but the line never says it's about the drawer. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: Bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer, from onboarding. The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: In the phrase 'waking from a ___,' the wrong answers 'flood' and 'war' don't make sense, so 'dream' is the only one that fits.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card re-tells Psalm 73:20, the same verse card 9 just asked about, with a joke added. It doesn't move the passage forward.
The card cites Psalm 73:21-22, but the right answer ('ignorant') comes from 73:22 only. Verse 21 is told only inside the choice card's question and has no story card.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: 'Asaph looks at the wicked one last time' says Psalm 73:27 is about the same wicked people as earlier. The verse speaks of 'Those far from You' and 'all who are unfaithful to You' and leaves that connection open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question reminds the baker that Asaph 'started out saying God is good,' and only the right answer repeats 'good' ('It is good to draw near to God'). The right answer stands out by its wording.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: A baker could argue the wrong answer 'It is safer to stay quiet' from Psalm 73:15, where Asaph holds back from speaking that way because it would betray God's children.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: 'From almost slipping to SINGING about it' says Asaph is singing. Psalm 73:28 says he will 'proclaim all Your works.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
